text:
anna: heads up — proposal to add a 'not:' prefix to the matcher grammar so we can express negation (e.g. not:query.foo=bar) and route by query params. cc @praveen @maria

praveen: this seems useful. couple concerns: how does negation interact with header overrides and the scoring/precedence model? also how will we show this in the console so customers aren't confused?

liam: implementation idea: grammar-level negation token. either treat not: as a filter applied after we build candidate set, or as a negative-scoring clause. leaning towards filter model to avoid weird score interactions.

maria: UX note — console needs an "explain match" trace that shows: candidate rules, which clauses matched, and which clauses filtered the request out. short, human readable.

anna: minimal grammar sketch for discussion:
```
match_clause := ["not:"] (host | path | header | query) ":" pattern
match := match_clause (" && " match_clause)*
```
this lets combos like: path:/signup && not:query.beta=true

dev-bot: matcher-unit-tests: running 48 tests against new grammar -> 12 failures (mostly around precedence semantics). see CI logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/matcher/7654

praveen: if we do filter semantics we must be careful about shadowing. e.g. a broad positive rule (service=* ) that matches earlier could prevent negation from having effect unless we evaluate filters globally. constraint approach: collect positives then filter.

liam: constraint approach is what I meant by candidate set. flow: 1) find positives by score threshold 2) apply negation filters 3) tie-break. pros: predictable, easy to explain; cons: could slightly increase eval cost and require more telemetry tagging.

ops-bot: perf report from small canary: enabling negation parsing on 20% of routes increased matcher p95 by ~1.8ms, p50 unchanged. memory overhead minimal. (run id: canary-2026-03-18-12)

maria: Console trace proposal: under route debug panel show:
- Candidate set (n)
- Matched clauses per rule (green/grey)
- Filtered by (negation clauses) with hover giving exact clause text
- Metric links: how often clause filtered requests
Also add a toggle "treat negation as constraint" vs "negation-as-score" in advanced route options for backwards-compatibility.

anna: agree on rollout: feature-flagged parser + trace fields, enable on canary, collect telemetry for candidate_count and negation_filter_hit counts. then enable by default after 2 weeks if no regressions.

liam: i'll take parser + unit tests, will open PR today and add opt-in flag. @maria can you own the trace UI mock and screenshots for the RFC?

maria: :thumbsup: i'll mock the UI and attach screenshots to the PR.

anna: thanks. next sync Friday EOD to review PR and canary numbers.
